decisions.reason: As a core printer platform very close to the firm's existing marking technology base, it fits strong in-house R&D and is likely to be refined rather than withdrawn.
The module builds directly on the firm's coding software capabilities and traceability offer, though as a narrower software add-on it has a somewhat higher discontinuation risk than core hardware.
An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces extends established application knowledge and is well within the firm's absorptive capacity, making continued commercialization likely.

The decoding app supports digitalization and traceability and even builds on a predecessor app, but as a more peripheral software tool outside the firm's main hardware-service core it is the most exposed to rationalization.
Inline code verification is tightly aligned with the firm's move toward serialization and end-to-end traceability, so its existing knowledge base should support learning and further rollout.
Print layout design software complements the installed base and common-operation strategy, and the firm's software and systems know-how makes retention more likely than exit.
